description_paragraphs: The set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is public, nonempty, closed, and convex, and may be unbounded. The operator $F$ is monotone and $\beta$-Lipschitz on $K$.

description_paragraphs: For a closed convex set $K$, define $N_K(z)=\{v:\langle v,u-z\rangle\le0,\ \forall u\in K\}$ for $z\in K$, and $\operatorname{dist}(0,S)=\inf_{v\in S}\|v\|_2$.
The tangent residual is finite at feasible points because $0\in N_K(z)$. This metric is not equal to $\|F(z)\|_2$.

bounds.derivation: The source hard domain can have diameter $R$, so any feasible public initial point is within $R$ of a solution. For every $v\in N_K(z)$, the local strong gap satisfies $\sup_{u\in K\cap B(z,1)}\langle F(z),z-u\rangle\le\|F(z)+v\|_2$, where $B(z,1)$ is the unit Euclidean ball centered at $z$. Taking the infimum over normal vectors converts the local-gap lower bound to a tangent-residual lower bound, preserving the quantifier over arbitrary deterministic algorithms.
bounds.lower_scope_type_note: The source theorem covers arbitrary adaptive deterministic queries, beyond linear-span iterations. It does not thereby give an arbitrary-randomized lower bound.

notes: Identify the source Lipschitz constant $L$ and distance bound $D_0$ with $\beta$ and $R$, respectively. The deterministic output criterion in source Section 2.2 is the tangent residual.

The local strong gap on $K\cap B(z,1)$ is bounded above by the tangent residual; $B(z,1)$ is the unit Euclidean ball. The source lower bound covers arbitrary deterministic operator-query algorithms and does not establish a randomized lower bound.
